## Purpose
Remote deployment targets. It covers create/read/update/delete of servers that receive tool code or workflow packages, the provider catalog, provider accounts (such as the Brev CLI login and cloud credentials), diagnostics, tool push, workflow package deployment and deployment history. On SSH servers it can also run console commands, build Docker stacks, delete deployed workflows and start runs on the server's worker.

## Responsibilities
- **Static paths**, declared before `/{server_id}`:
  - `GET /remote-servers/providers` returns `providers.catalog()`: the server kinds, their fields, and the workflow post-deploy actions.
  - `GET /remote-servers/accounts` returns the login state of every account provider, checked in parallel threads.
  - `GET /remote-servers/accounts/{provider}`; an `AccountError` becomes 404.
  - `POST .../{provider}/login` takes `{values{field: value}, remember?}`. The legacy `{token, org}` body is also accepted. Cloud credentials are always stored, encrypted; a CLI token only when `remember` is set.
  - `POST .../{provider}/start` takes `{ref}` and starts a stopped cloud VM.
  - `POST .../{provider}/org` and `.../logout`. An `AccountError` on these becomes 422.
  - `GET /remote-servers?purpose=` lists servers newest first, via `store.to_dict`.
  - `POST /remote-servers`:
    1. the name is required (422);
    2. `_parse_body` accepts the structured body and the legacy `{name, url, description}`; the default provider is `mcp_code_endpoint`, and purpose `tool` for that provider, else `workflow`;
    3. `store.normalise` validates (a `ValidationError` becomes 422);
    4. secrets are encrypted with `secret_box`;
    5. `url` is set to `store.display_address`;
    6. an `initial_check` result from the add form is saved as the first diagnostics;
    7. provisioned providers (Brev) start `deployers.start_brev_provision` and return `provision_deployment_id`.
  - `POST /remote-servers/test` runs diagnostics on unsaved settings. With `server_id`, blank secrets fall back to the stored ones and the known host fingerprint is kept. A validation failure returns an "unreachable" report with a failing `config` check.
  - `POST /remote-servers/check-all?purpose=` checks every server concurrently (a semaphore of 6), reports progress ("Checked X: status"), saves each result and returns `{summary{healthy, degraded, unreachable}, results}`.
  - `POST /remote-servers/check` is a legacy bare-URL reachability check.
  - `GET /remote-servers/deployments/{id}`.
  - `POST .../deployments/{id}/cancel`:
    - only `command` deployments can be stopped (422 otherwise);
    - a running command is cancelled and returns `{status: "stopping"}`;
    - a queued or running row that nothing in this process runs any more is marked failed ("Not running any more — stopped tracking it") and returns `{status: "cleared"}`;
    - otherwise 409 "This command has already finished".
  - `GET /remote-servers/deployments?workflow_name&limit≤200` returns recent deployments with `server_name` and without logs.
- **A single server:**
  - `GET` and `DELETE`, which also deletes the server's deployment rows.
  - `PUT`:
    - merges `config` and `url`;
    - normalises, with the stored secrets as fallback;
    - keeps the stored SSH host key only when host, port and provider are unchanged;
    - resets `last_status` when the connection or any secret changed.
  - `POST /{id}/check` runs full diagnostics and saves them.
  - `POST /{id}/provision` works only for provisioned types (422 otherwise); a `DeployError` becomes 409.
  - `POST /{id}/commands` (SSH only) takes `{command | preset, workflow?, timeout=600}` and starts `deployers.start_remote_command`.
  - `POST /{id}/build` (SSH) takes `{workflow (required), services=["backend"], no_cache, pull, run_bootstrap, start=true, force_recreate, remove_orphans, build_args, env}`. It calls `build_compose_command` and then `start_remote_command(timeout=3600, action="build", env=clean_env(env))`.
  - `POST /{id}/delete-workflow` (SSH) takes `{workflow, confirm, stop_containers=true, remove_volumes, remove_images}`. `confirm` must repeat the workflow name (422 "Type the workflow name to confirm the deletion"). The command runs in the deploy directory.
  - `POST /{id}/run-workflow` (SSH) takes `{workflow, input{}, deployment_name?}`; see Key elements.
  - `GET /{id}/remote-workflows` returns the workflows unpacked on an SSH server, with their containers, or `{supported: false}`.
  - `GET /{id}/deployments` returns the last 50.
  - `POST /{id}/send-tool` takes `{tool_id}` and works only for `purpose=tool` servers; other cases return a soft `{status: "error"}`.
  - `POST /{id}/deploy-workflow` takes `{workflow_name, ...options}` and works only for `purpose=workflow` servers; a `DeployError` becomes 409.

## Key elements
- **`_save_check(db, server, result)`:**
  1. Refreshes the row first, because a Brev check may have saved re-resolved settings from another session.
  2. Saves the status, the JSON report and the time.
  3. Remembers the SSH host fingerprint the first time it is seen (trust on first use).
- **`run-workflow`:**
  1. Checks the required inputs against the local definition.
  2. Reads the workflow's `.env` on the server (`deployers.remote_env_info`) to get `deployment_name` and the key's hash.
  3. Refuses with 422 when there is no `DEPLOYMENT_NAME`, no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, or a key hash different from this app's key. A worker with a different key polls another workspace and would never pick the run up.
  4. Warns when this app's own worker also polls that deployment name.
  5. Calls `routes.workflows.mistral_execute(workflow, inputs, deployment)`.
  6. Returns `{execution_id, status, workflow_name, deployment_name, warnings}`.

## Control flow
Long operations return a `RemoteDeployment` row. The UI polls `GET /remote-servers/deployments/{id}` for its status and log.

## Data, state and side effects
- The `remote_servers`, `remote_deployments` and `remote_provider_accounts` tables.
- SSH connections and remote commands (paramiko, in the deployers).
- Brev CLI calls and cloud APIs.
- Mistral workflow executions.

## Configuration
`MISTRAL_WORKER_ENABLED`.

## Interactions
- Route policy: remote_servers.view for GET and remote_servers.manage for writes.
- Uses `app/remote_servers/*`.
- Used by the frontend Remote Servers page and the workflow Deploy dialog.

## Error handling and edge cases
See Responsibilities. Without a database most routes return 503 "Database not available"; the list returns `[]`.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **Route order matters.** The static paths are declared first so `/{server_id}` does not capture them.
## How to rebuild this file
The helpers and handlers above, in the same order.

## Tests
None.
